action: Apply Fortinet's updates to FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiSASE, FortiPAM and FortiSandbox after testing, and administer them from segmented systems that are not internet-connected.
exec: A large Fortinet patch batch with no known exploitation; plan prompt but orderly updates, starting with management consoles.
plain: Fortinet released fixes for dozens of flaws in its firewall and management products. No attacks are known yet, but the worst could let an intruder take control.

key_findings: Affected products include FortiOS 8.0.0-8.0.1 and 7.6.0-7.6.7, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0-8.0.2, FortiSASE, FortiPAM and FortiSandbox, plus older branches.
The advisory lists 46 CVEs, 37 of them in FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer.
The most severe flaws could allow arbitrary code execution, with impact depending on the privileges of the affected account.
No exploitation in the wild had been reported at publication.
Risk is rated High for government and business entities of every size and Low for home users.
recommendations: Apply Fortinet's updates to vulnerable systems immediately after appropriate testing.
Keep network infrastructure on current, supported software and remediate detected vulnerabilities at least monthly.
Apply least privilege and disable or secure default accounts.
Use dedicated, segmented, non-internet-connected systems for administrative work.

summary: MS-ISAC advisory 2026-133 covers 46 CVEs across Fortinet products, most in FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, with others in FortiOS, FortiSASE and FortiSandbox. The most severe could let an attacker run arbitrary code and, depending on account privileges, install programs, alter data or create accounts. No exploitation was reported at publication. Risk is rated High for government and business of all sizes.
title: MS-ISAC: Fortinet FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer flaws could allow arbitrary code execution

validation.note: Reviewed against the original MS-ISAC document.
